Now, we must also consider the observation of the **configurations** <term>configurations: 'schematismoi,' the geometric relationships between the stars</term>. For just as the placement of the wandering stars <note>original: "planōmenōn," the source of our word 'planets'</note> throughout the entire zodiacal circle establishes their particular powers, so too does the **Moon** (☽). From her rising <note>the New Moon</note> until the **first quarter** <term>first quarter: original 'dichotomou,' literally 'cut in half'</term>, she is more productive of moisture. From the first quarter until the **full moon** <note>original: "panselēnou"</note>, she is more productive of heat. From the full moon until the **second quarter**, she produces dryness. And finally, from the second quarter until her **hidden phase** <note>original: "krypseōs," the conjunction with the Sun</note>, she produces coldness. 

The planets, when they are matutine <term>matutine: rising in the morning before the Sun; original 'heōoi'</term>, also have phases: from their rising until the **first station** <term>first station: the point where a planet appears to stop before turning retrograde</term>, they are more moistening; from the first station until the **acronychal rising** <term>acronychal rising: 'akronykton,' when a planet rises exactly as the Sun sets, being in opposition</term>, they are more heating; from the acronychal rising until the **second station**, they are more drying; and from the second station until their setting, they are more cooling. ## On the Power of the Fixed Stars

<margin><image-desc>Red cross and ornamental flourish</image-desc></margin> Since this cycle [the Zodiac] also concerns the nature of the **fixed stars** <note>original: "aplanon asteron," stars that do not "wander" like planets</note>, we shall now run through their specific qualities. We will set forth the observed peculiarities of each star and the ways they have shown themselves to be similar to the natures of the **planets** <note>original: "planomenon," the wanderers</note>. It is as follows:

Regarding those stars belonging to **Aries** <note>the Ram</note> that share in the nature of the constellation <unclear>...</unclear> those in the **head** have an active power blended from the qualities of **Mars** (♂) and the **Moon** (☽). Those in the **mouth** are influenced by **Jupiter** (♃) and partly by **Mars** (♂). Those on the **hind foot** have the power of the **Fiery One** <term>Fiery One: "pyroentos," a traditional Greek name for the planet Mars</term>. Those on the **tail** share the power of **Venus** (♀).

Of those stars in **Taurus** <note>the Bull</note>, those on the **section** <note>original: "apotome"; Taurus is traditionally depicted as only the front half of a bull</note> have a temperament similar to **Venus** (♀) and partly **Saturn** (♄). Of the stars in **Gemini** <note>the Twins</note>, those at the **feet** share the same quality as **Mercury** (☿) and partly **Venus** (♀). **T**he bright stars around the **thighs** are like **Jupiter** (♃). Of the stars in **Cancer** <note>the Crab</note>, the two on the **feet** produce the same active influence as **Mercury** (☿).

### **The Four Seasons of the Year**

**S**uch, then, are the powers of the stars themselves as recorded by the observations of the ancients. Regarding the conditions of the seasons of the year, their qualities are derived from the changes they undergo. **Spring** is moist because, as the cold of the past winter passes and the heat begins, there is a diffusion of water into the air as it warms. This occurs as the **Sun** approaches the point directly over our heads <note>the zenith</note>. **Summer** is dry because of the heat and the consumption of moisture by the scorching temperatures that have passed. **Autumn** is dry and cold because the Sun has withdrawn furthest from the point over our heads. **Winter** is cold because of the lack of intense heat. Since there is no fixed beginning in a circle, the twelfth-part of the zodiac beginning from the **Spring Equinox**, which is **Aries**, is assumed to be the start, just as if it were a living being.

<summary>This page concludes the list of fixed stars' planetary temperaments for the southern constellations and explains the elemental qualities (heat, moisture, etc.) of the four seasons. It establishes the Spring Equinox in Aries as the logical starting point for the astrological year.</summary>

<keywords>Canis Major, Sirius, Centaurus, Corvus, Argo Navis, seasons, Spring Equinox, Aries, elemental qualities, moisture, heat</keywords>

--- Page 686 ---
<meta>This page continues the discussion initiated on the previous page regarding the physical characteristics of the seasons, transitioning into a comparison between the stages of human life and the four quarters of the horizon (the cardinal directions).</meta>

<margin>
Regarding the
[parts] of the
occurring
center-points :-
</margin>

In the cycle of the zodiac, one makes the transition of **spring** the starting point. The remaining seasons follow in order, because the first age of all living beings—much like the essence of **spring**—possesses an abundance of moisture. For in their beginning, young creatures are tender and moist. The second age, which lasts until the peak of life, possesses an abundance of heat, corresponding to **summer**. The third age, which is already past the peak and at the beginning of decline, has a greater share of dryness, similar to **autumn**. The final age, nearing the "setting" of life <note>a metaphor for death, comparing a lifespan to a single day</note>, is characterized by cold, just as **winter** is.

<image-desc>A small red circle with a center dot used as a paragraph or section separator.</image-desc>

Similarly, one observes these qualities in the regions of the horizon. The starting points of the winds appear to follow this same logic. The region toward the **East** <note>original: "anatolai"</note> possesses more dryness. This is because whatever moisture was produced during the night is dried by the sun as it "cooks" the earth upon rising. The winds blowing from this direction, which we more commonly call **Apeliotes** <term>Apeliotes</term> <note>the East Wind, often depicted in Greek art as a young man carrying fruit or grain</note>, are without moisture and are drying in nature.

The region toward the **South** <note>original: "mesembria"</note> is the hottest because of the fiery nature of the sun’s **mid-heaven passages** <term>mesouranesis</term> <note>the point when the sun reaches its highest point in the sky at noon</note>. Furthermore, because of the inclination of our **inhabited world** <term>oikoumene</term> <note>the portion of the Earth known to the ancients, specifically the Northern Hemisphere</note>, the sun's path inclines more toward the south. The winds blowing from there, which we commonly call **Notoi** <note>original: "notoi", the South Winds</note>, are hot and "filling" <note>original: "plerotikoi"; this may refer to the heavy, thick air often associated with southerly winds</note>.

The region toward the **West** <note>original: "dusmai"</note> is the most moist. This is because the air is cooled and moistened during the sun's rest after the duration of the day. The winds moving from this direction, which we more commonly call **Zephyrs** <term>Zephyroi</term> <note>the West Winds, associated with spring breezes and moisture</note>, are fresh and moistening.

The region toward the **North** <note>original: "arktoi", literally "the Bears", referring to the northern constellations</note> is the coldest. This is because, according to the inclination of our inhabited world, the sun’s mid-heaven passages—which are the cause of heat—are furthest removed from this region, as if the sun were culminating in the opposite direction. The winds from the North, then, are cold and have a condensing effect <note>original: "pyknotikoi" — referring to the physical process of making matter more dense through cooling</note>. [There is] already a separation of these factors in order to distinguish the specific mixtures of each individual place. This is easily understood through the stations <term>staseis</term> and phases <term>phaseis</term> <note>referring to when a planet appears to stop or change direction in the sky</note> of the stars, or their age and lineage. Furthermore, consider the productive power of the stars' influence: for in their own proper configurations, they possess their quality in a more unmixed state, and in their activity, they are more effective.

For those stars in hot regions possess a hot nature, while in moist regions they are moisture-producing. In the opposite regions, they have a mixed and weaker nature—just as in cold regions they do not remain hot, and in dry regions they are not moist. This applies to the other qualities as well; the quality produced through this mixing is not uniform.

...tropical signs, and the opposites of the winter signs. There are also two equinoctial signs. Of the remaining eight twelfth-parts, four are called "solid" <term>sterea</term> <note>now commonly known in astrology as "Fixed" signs</note> and four are called "double-bodied" <term>disōma</term> <note>now known as "Mutable" signs</note>. The solid signs are those that follow the tropical and equinoctial signs: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius. These are so named because when the Sun is in them, the qualities of the seasons that began in the preceding signs—whether they be the changing weather, heat, dryness, or cold—reach us more powerfully and "solidly." This is not because the natural conditions are intrinsically more temperate at that time, but because we have already grown accustomed to them and therefore feel their established strength more than we feel the initial shock of the change in our bodies.

The double-bodied signs are those that follow the solid signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces. They are called this because they lie between the solid and the tropical signs, and they share, as it were, the natural properties of both seasonal states at their beginnings and ends.

Similarly, certain segments are called **hearing** <term>akouonta</term> and **obeying** <term>hypakouonta</term>. They say that all signs have **equal power** <note>original: "isodynamein" — having equal strength or influence</note> which are perceived as being at an equal distance from the same points of the **equator** <term>isēmerinos</term> <note>the celestial equator, the Great Circle that represents the projection of the Earth's equator into space</note> and the **pole**. However, those segments are called **disjunct** <note>original: "allotriōmena" — alienated or estranged</note> which have absolutely no relationship to one another based on the familiarities we have described. These are the signs that are neither "commanding" nor "hearing," nor are they "beholding" or "having equal power." Furthermore, they are those that fall outside the four established configurations: the **opposition** <note>original: "diamesos" — 180 degrees apart</note>, the **trine** <note>120 degrees apart</note>, the **square** <note>90 degrees apart</note>, and the **hexagon** <note>the 60-degree sextile</note>. Those separated by five signs <note>150 degrees apart, known today as a quincunx</note> divide the entire circle into unequal parts, whereas the other aspects make a division that is a proportional fraction of the circumference. <margin>+ <insert>familiar stars</insert></margin>

The planets are associated with the parts of the zodiac through what are called **houses**, as well as through **triangles**, **exaltations**, **bounds**, and the like. The system of "houses" has a natural explanation of this sort: since the most northern of the twelve signs are those that approach closest to our zenith <note>the point directly overhead</note> and are therefore most capable of producing heat and sharpness, namely **Cancer** <term>karkinos</term> and **Leo** <term>leōn</term>, they assigned these two to the greatest and most sovereign bodies. ...in considering one <gloss>each</gloss> of these matters, it is much more necessary to have first grasped those that are of a more general nature. This nature is not detached from the physical circumstances of the stars and the signs of the zodiac that share an affinity with them.

<meta>This page continues Ptolemy's discussion on the "familiarity" (oikeiosis) between the heavens and the earth. Having established that the stars influence whole regions, he now moves into a proto-ethnographic description of how the sun's path determines the physical and temperamental characteristics of different human populations based on their latitude.</meta>

It is said that those who live between the equator and the summer tropic <term>equator and summer tropic</term> <note>The "summer tropic" refers to the Tropic of Cancer. Ptolemy is describing the tropical zone.</note> have the sun directly overhead <note>original: ἐπὶ κορυφὴν; literally "at the peak" or zenith</note> and are scorched by the heat. Their bodies are blackened and their hair is curly or woolly <note>original: οὐλοτρίχας</note>. Their physical forms are stunted and their temperaments are hot; in their character, they are generally quite wild due to the constant, oppressive heat of the regions where they live. We commonly call these people Ethiopians <note>original: αἰθίοπας; meaning "burnt-faced ones." In antiquity, this term referred to various dark-skinned peoples of Sub-Saharan Africa.</note>. For they are named according to this condition. Moreover, the state of the air that surrounds them and the plants found in their regions clearly reflect these same conditions.

<margin>☉</margin> As for those in the more northern latitudes <term>parallels</term>—I mean those living under the region of the Bears <note>The constellations Ursa Major and Minor, used to mark the north</note>—they have the celestial pole almost directly overhead. They are far removed from the zodiac <term>zodiac</term> <note>the path of the sun and planets</note> and the heat of the sun. Consequently, they are continually chilled. They possess a much fairer skin color, and unlike those in the tropics, they are not <unclear>stunted</unclear> but rather tall. Their complexions are very white, their hair is fine and straight, and their bodies are large and well-developed in size. In their physical nature, they are "moist" <note>In ancient medicine, a "moist" or "phlegmatic" temperament was associated with growth and cold climates.</note>. They, too, are wild in character, because their dwelling places are subjected to constant cold. The wintry state of the air around them follows this same pattern, as do the plants of those regions. We generally call these people 
<margin>λ</margin> Scythians <note>original: σκύθας; a term used for the nomadic peoples of the northern steppes</note>.

<margin>☉ ¶</margin> For those living between the summer tropic and the region of the Bears, the sun is never directly overhead, nor does it move too far away from the zenith during its midday passage. They are said to enjoy a temperate climate <term>temperate</term> <note>original: εὐκρασίας; literally a "good mixing" or balance of the elements</note>. This climate does not fluctuate with extremes, nor do they suffer from excessive cold. In complexion, they are of a medium hue; in stature, they are moderate; in their physical natures, they are well-balanced; and their settlements are likewise temperate.

And of the Aegean sea; since, therefore, in my own mind [the regions] are divided simply, or as part of a map, there are four **quadrants** <note>original: τεταρτημόρια (tetartēmoria); the four quarters of the world based on the intersection of the horizon and the meridian.</note> that correspond to the positions of the **triplicities** <note>original: τριγώνων (trigonōn); also called "triangles," these are groups of three zodiac signs that share an elemental nature.</note>. Of these, the first is the northern quadrant of the whole **inhabited world** <note>original: οἰκουμένης (oikoumenēs); the world known to the Greeks.</note>, situated near our [sea], which we commonly call **Europe**. Opposite to this, and toward the South-East <note>original: νότον ἀπηλιώτην; the direction of the south and the east wind combined.</note>, is the region by the Red Sea, which would be called the southern part of **Great Asia**. Alternately, toward the North-East of the whole inhabited world is the region near **Scythia**, which is itself the northern part of Great Asia. The quadrant opposite to this, lying toward the South-West wind <note>original: λίβα νότον; Libs is the southwest wind, and Notos is the south wind.</note>, is the region toward the West and the [Atlantic] Ocean, which we commonly call **Libya** <note>The ancient name for the continent of Africa.</note>. <note>Abbreviation for Περιέχουσι</note> Each of these regions, as they are situated in a quadrant, has a position contrary to those reckoned toward the southern parts of the whole inhabited world, according to the quadrant that contains it, so that it may encompass the whole inhabited world.

The region of **Europe**, being situated toward the north of the whole inhabited world, stands opposite to the parts near the meridian. As for the South-East, that quadrant belongs to those who already possess a [celestial] sphere; and it is now similar, so that from this, each of the quadrants is made familiar to the opposite interior angles [of the triplicities]. Just as some parts [are assigned] according to that which is being applied. As for the part near the meridian or the opposite portion, these are included as part of the **familiarity** <note>original: οἰκείωσιν (oikeiōsin); the astrological affinity between a geographical region and a zodiacal sign or planet.</note>. If the planets hold the **rulership** <note>original: οἰκοδεσποτείαν; literally "acting as master of the house."</note> over their own interior angles, then the familiarity concerns them alone. Since it is either about the part of the inhabited world, that too is the [nature of] heat. On account of this arrangement, the parts of the aforementioned quadrants exist according to such a distribution.

Let us speak of the part [concerning] **Europe**. The regions lying toward the North-Northwest of the whole **inhabited world** <note>original: οἰκουμένης (oikoumenēs)</note> are associated with the North-Northwest **triplicity** <note>original: τριγώνῳ (trigonō); here referring to the "Fire" signs: Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius.</note>—that of **Aries**, **Leo**, and **Sagittarius**. As is natural, this region is ruled by the lords of that triplicity: **Jupiter** [♃] and **Mars** [♂] in their **evening positions** <note>original: ἑσπερίων (hesperiōn); referring to planets that rise and set after the Sun.</note>. 

From these influences, the nations within the whole area are called:
- **Britain**
- **Galatia** <note>Likely referring here to Gaul (modern France) or the Celtic regions generally.</note>
- **Germany**
- **Bastarnia** <note>An ancient territory in the region of the Carpathian Mountains.</note>
- **Italy**
- **Gaul**
- **Apulia**
- **Sicily**
- **Tyrrhenia** <note>Etruria, or Western Italy.</note>
- **Celtica**
- **Spain**

As a result, it has generally coincided that the nations living there—because of the dominant nature of these triplicities and the stars that rule them together—are unsubdued, liberty-loving, fond of arms, industrious, very warlike, and naturally inclined toward leadership; they are also clean and high-minded. This is due to the evening configuration of **Jupiter** [♃] and **Mars** [♂].

Furthermore, because the front parts of these particular triplicities are highly masculine and the latter parts are feminine, it happens that [these peoples] are indifferent toward women and contemptuous of sexual relations [with them]. However, they are more insatiable and quite jealous regarding the company of males. Among those so disposed, they do not consider what occurs to be shameful, nor do they truly become unmanly or soft because of this <note>Ptolemy is describing the customs of the northern "barbarian" tribes as he understood them, attributing their sexual behaviors to planetary alignments.</note>; for the masculine influence does not allow for a passive state. Instead, they preserve their souls for courage, community, loyalty, affection, and benevolence.

Regarding these specific lands:
- **Britain**, **Galatia**, **Germany**, and **Bastarnia** are more closely associated with **Aries** and **Mars** [♂]; hence, those who live in these places generally happen to be more fierce, self-willed, and bestial. 
- **Italy**, **Apulia**, **Spain**, and **Sicily** are associated with **Leo** and the **Sun** [☉]; for this reason, these peoples are more inclined toward leadership and are more benevolent. 
- **Tyrrhenia** and **Celtica** [are associated with Sagittarius...]

**Cappadocia** is associated with the star of **Jupiter** [♃]; whence comes the peoples' love of liberty, their simplicity, and their love of cleanliness. <gloss>paragraph</gloss> And as for the parts in the southern region, around the southern division of the **inhabited world** <note>original: οἰκουμένης (oikoumenēs)</note>, these include **Thrace**, **Macedonia**, **Illyria**, **Greece**, **Achaia**, and **Crete**; and furthermore, the **Cyclades** islands, the coastal regions of **Asia Minor**, and **Cyprus**.

These regions, lying toward the South and the East <note>original: ἀπηλιώτην (apēliōtēn), the East wind</note>, are assigned to the **second triplicity** <note>The "Earth" triplicity consisting of Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn.</note>, which is associated with the East and with the star of **Mercury** [☿]. This is due to the signs of **Taurus**, **Virgo**, and **Capricorn**. Furthermore, there is a shared dominion by the stars of **Venus** [♀], **Mercury** [☿], and **Saturn** [♄].

Therefore, those who inhabit these lands have generally turned out to be more controlled and balanced <note>original: κεκραμένοι (kekramenoi); literally "tempered" or "mixed," referring to a harmonious temperament.</note> in both their bodies and their souls. They are:
- **Leadership-oriented**, headstrong, fond of physical exercise, and somewhat subtle <note>original: ὑπόπλοκοι (hypoplokoi); meaning crafty or complex in thought.</note> because of **Saturn** [♄].
- **Liberty-loving**, yet also prone to tyranny, democracy, and the establishment of laws because of **Jupiter** [♃].
- **Lovers of music** and learning, fond of competition, and clean in their habits of life because of **Venus** [♀].
- **Sociable**, hospitable, lovers of justice, fond of letters, and exceptionally eloquent because of **Mercury** [☿].
- They are also keepers of **mysteries** because of the **evening configuration** <note>Referring to the planet's position relative to the Sun.</note> of **Venus** [♀].

<gloss>paragraph</gloss> In particular, the distribution <note>original: ἀπόνοια (aponoia); likely a scribal variant for "assignment" or "character."</note> for the **Cyclades**, the coastal regions of **Asia Minor**, and **Cyprus** is more closely associated with **Taurus** and **Venus** [♀]. Consequently, these people are for the most part cautious, lovers of cleanliness, and take great care of their physical bodies. 

However, those in the regions of **Greece**, **Achaia**, and **Crete** are associated with **Virgo** and **Mercury** [☿]. For this reason, they happen to be more rational and fond of learning, and they cultivate the virtues of the soul even before those of the body.

These people are **passionate** and **lecherous**, and they are prone to indulgence in sexual pleasures. They are fond of **dancing** and **leaping**, and they love **finery** and ornaments because of the influence of **Venus** [♀]. However, they live **luxuriously** because of **Saturn** [♄]. Because of these influences, many of them have sexual relations and bear children with their own **mothers**. Most of them practice a form of worship that is <unclear>religious</unclear> or pious toward the **Rising Sun** <note>The dawn or the East.</note>, because the heart—the ruling part of the soul—is naturally attuned to the power of the **Sun** [☉]. In general, these characteristics are reflected in their clothing, their ornaments, and their entire physical appearance.

Having thus set forth these matters, it would follow next to go over the methods of <term>prognostication</term> <note>original: προτελέσεων (proteleseōn) – predictions or foretelling of events</note> in a summary fashion. <meta>This page transitions from the geographical list of regions to the methodological framework for predicting the effects of eclipses. It establishes three levels of inquiry: the timing/duration, the general regions affected, and the specific outcomes.</meta>

-> + <-

The time of the <term>portents</term> <note>original: ἐπισημασιῶν (episemasiōn) – significant celestial events, particularly those indicating future changes</note>, and the quantity of their duration, must also be discerned. Second is the general consideration, by which it is proper to determine which classes of people the event will befall. Finally, there is the specific consideration, by which we shall observe the outcome produced under this [method]. +

<margin>1</margin> We shall therefore give our account of the first and most general topic, which is of the following sort. That one alone is the ruler. 

But if the same star is not found to be ruler of both the eclipse and the angle, we must take the one that has the most numerous and <margin>x</margin> most significant relationships to both by way of **familiarity** <note>original: συνοικειώσει (synoikeiōsei) — the technical kinship or affinity between a planet and a specific part of the zodiac</note>. If many are found to be equally matched in each category, we prefer the one that is more dominant or has more **influence** <note>original: χρηματιστικώτερον (chrēmatistikōteron) — literally "profitable" or "effective," referring to a star in a strong, active position</note>, especially one belonging to the **sect** <note>original: αἱρέσεως (haireseōs) — the division of planets into day and night groups</note> of the ruler.

# The Influence of the Ruling Stars and Their Qualities

And [the effect] of the **lordship** <term>lordship: (oikodespoteia) the state of a planet being the "master" or ruler of a specific zodiac sign or astrological house</term> of the stars depends on the strength or weakness of those who have held that lordship. For the study of the **temperament** <term>temperament: (krasis) the specific blending of hot, cold, wet, and dry qualities that define a planet's nature</term> of those who have taken control reveals the power of the quality of all results. We shall begin with the productive property of each of the **planets** <note>original: πλανωμένων (planōmenōn) — literally "the wanderers," referring to the five known planets plus the Sun and Moon</note>, setting this out generally first: for the sake of a summary reminder, one must assume the whole general influence emitted from them toward the temperament, considering the variety within a similar nature. This applies whether the planetary condition is in its own sign, or in those that are declining, or in the zodiac according to its own specific temperament.

Regarding the present matters—the natures, the qualities, and the names given to the stars—and the qualities found in their blendings, one must consider not only the mixture of unlike things with each other, but also those that share the same nature. For the positions of the stars in the zodiac, according to their demonstrated relationships, bring about a universal affinity of all things.

When a planet that is uniform and of one mind <note>likely referring to a planet acting alone or being in a sign that perfectly matches its nature</note> takes the lordship, it acts universally against external causes. Specifically, it encompasses the body's condition, bringing about **long-lasting diseases**. It causes these continually in discharges; and in the final stages, it brings **rheumatism** <gloss>bodily fluxes or "runny" conditions</gloss>, and **elephantine manifestations** <note>original: ἐλεφαντιακὰς (elephantian) — likely referring to leprosy or elephantiasis, diseases that thicken the skin</note>, as well as inflammations and outflows, and continuous fevers, fear, and deaths. 

These effects occur especially in those of advanced age. For in this way, they also give painful weakness to animals regarding their secretions, causing bodily destruction and disease. In places inhabited by **speechless animals** <gloss>literally "the voiceless," meaning livestock or wild animals</gloss>, they cause destruction within a month. Regarding the state of the air, it brings **fearful colds**, frosty and misty, from which arise **pestilences** <note>original: λοιποί (loimoi) — plague or infectious disease</note>, foul air, cloudiness, and gloom. For women, it brings a multitude of diseases and a destructive number of deaths. It also brings the destruction of all kinds of speechless and afflicted reptiles.

*   The **Spring Equinox** <note>original: ἐαρινὸν ἰσημερινόν (earinon isēmerinon)</note>: This is chosen because it is the first time the **day begins to be longer than the night**. *   The **Summer Solstice** <note>original: θερινὸν τροπικόν (therinon tropikon)</note>: This is chosen because the **longest day** is completed at this point. Moreover, for the **Egyptians** <note>original: Αἰγυπτίους (Aigyptious)</note>, it signifies the **rising of the Nile** <note>original: Νείλου ἀνάβασιν (Neilou anabasin)</note> and the rising of the **Dog Star** <note>original: κυνὸς ἄστρου (kynos astrou) — the star Sirius, which heralded the flooding of the Nile</note>.

*   The **Autumn Equinox** <note>original: μετοπωρινὸν ἰσημερινόν (metopōrinon isēmerinon)</note>: This is chosen because all things have by now reached [completion]...

<meta>This page marks a major transition in the manuscript, moving from Book II (universal/mundane astrology) to Book III (individual/genethlialogical astrology). It establishes the philosophical link between general cosmic events and the specific fate of individuals.</meta>

Having traversed in what went before <note>original: ἐν τοῖς ἔμπροσθεν (en tois emprosthen) — referring to the previous sections of the work</note> the theory of **universal occurrences** <term>symptomatic theory</term> <note>original: συμπτωματικῆς θεωρίας (symptomatikēs theōrias) — the study of general events like eclipses, plagues, or weather patterns affecting entire regions</note>, we now approach that which is primarily and most powerfully able to govern the specific nature of every individual human being. We must consider this part of **prognostic** <term>prognostic</term> knowledge to have its origin and path from one and the same power that governs both types of prediction. 

Furthermore, regarding both the universal and the theoretical: since in both universal symptoms and those concerning each individual, the cause is the movement of the **wandering stars** <term>planets</term> <note>original: πλανωμένων ἀστέρων (planōmenōn asterōn) — the ancient term for the planets, including the Sun and Moon</note>, the sun, and the moon. This constitutes the prognostic science of their underlying nature in their most general passages; thus, a **scientific observation** <note>original: ἐπιστημονικὴ παρατήρησις (epistēmonikē paratērēsis)</note> has been preserved throughout the ages. 

Except that while the **universal circumstance** <term>universal</term> <note>original: καθολικὴ περίστασις (katholikē peristasis) — circumstances affecting the world or whole nations</note> is greater and more self-sufficient, the particular case does not possess its principles in the same manner. Nevertheless, both are regarded as the foundations from which one must construct the theory of the cause of all things. The signs indicated by individual bodies may be known long in advance, yet the particular parts are governed by the same movement as the universal wholes. These signs are not always derived from the underlying subjects themselves, but from the **surroundings** <note>original: περιεχόντων (periechontōn) — literally "the things that surround," referring to the heavens and the atmosphere</note> which bring about almost all the causes from the more perfect and well-tempered movements of the significant passing stars we observe. 

We now focus our attention on each individual person, and we take this [divine] governance as our starting point. For in many ways, the prognostications of the surroundings occur around significant turning points, following the one primary **impression at birth** <term>geniture</term> <note>original: γενέσεως ἀποτύπωσιν (geneseōs apotypōsin) — the "stamping" or "imprinting" of the soul and body by celestial influences at the moment of birth</note>, and this brings the others to fulfillment. For those so constituted from the first beginning, the power of their **constitution** <term>complexion</term> <note>original: συγκρίσεως (synkriseōs) — the unique mixture of physical and spiritual qualities</note> is observed through the things that follow according to the seasons and the events that occur.

Looking at it closely, this formation is a rule or, if it seems so, a worthy account containing the internal development <note>original: ἔντεξιν (entexin) — the internal gestation or "bearing" within</note> or even an accidental occurrence. For this very thing is a specific and proper characteristic of the superior formation toward nature; it happens to be something divine. After the completion of nature, this occurs so that the foundations are not merely underlying materials, but are the original transformations.

### On the Longevity of the Parents

Regarding the **father** <gloss>original abbreviation: πρ̄ς (patros)</gloss>, one must form an assessment. If the parents are weakened, and not only that but also very **short-lived**, it is when the star of **Jupiter** <note>original: Διός (Dios)</note> does not preside, nor does any benefic planet **overcome** <term>kathyperterēsis|A dominant astrological position where a planet is in the 10th sign relative to another, "ruling" over it from above</term> the **Sun** or the star of **Saturn** <gloss>♄</gloss>. This is true even if a planet rises after them, or if Saturn himself is not in harmony with the Sun, but is instead in **opposition** <gloss>diameter</gloss> or **square** <term>tetragon|An aspect of 90 degrees, usually considered stressful or challenging</term>, and especially if they are not positioned in the **centers** <term>kentra|The four pivotal points of a chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Lower Midheaven</term>. In such cases, they produce only weak lives.

However, regarding **Saturn** <gloss>♄</gloss>, if he is succeeding the centers, he makes the fathers short-lived or **injured** <note>original: ἐπισινεῖς (episineis) — referring to bodily harm, disabilities, or impairments</note>. We see that they are short-lived when the planets are in the centers or even declining from them. Those that have declined, those in the Midheaven, or those in the houses succeeding them <note>The "succedent" houses follow the "angular" centers and provide them with support or momentum</note> dictate these outcomes. They produce **sickly** <note>original: ἐπινόσους (epinosous)</note> or injured parents when they are in the remaining centers—specifically the **Setting** angle <gloss>the West or Descendant</gloss> and the **Underworld** angle <gloss>the IC or lowest point of the sky</gloss>—or in the houses succeeding these.

Just as when the star of Saturn looks upon the Sun in the manner we have described, he suddenly destroys the father or causes things like **convulsions** <note>original: περιταράγματα (peritaragmata) — sudden disturbances or physical shocks</note>. If he looks upon the star of Saturn <note>referring to a transit or aspectual relationship</note>, he causes deaths or **fevers with chills** <note>original: ῥιγοπυρέτους (rhigopyretous)</note>, or injuries to the limbs through his movements. Beyond this, he himself causes **shameful misfortune** in relation to the Sun, and he brings about deaths that follow lingering illnesses, or general suffering through the **affliction** <note>original: καχώσεως (kachōseōs) — a state of planetary debility or "bad condition"</note> of the signs.

### Regarding the Mother

Regarding the **mother** <gloss>original abbreviation: μρ̄ς (mētros)</gloss>: if the **Moon** <gloss>☾</gloss> does not have any assistance from **Venus** <gloss>♀</gloss> in any way whatsoever, or if Venus herself is not in harmony with the Moon—by being in a **square**, or a **trine** <term>trigon|A harmonious aspect of 120 degrees</term>, or conjoined with her—it is the strengthening of these relationships that proclaims the **longevity** <note>original: πολυχρονίαν (polychronian)</note> of the mother.

But if the star of **Mars** <note>original: Ἄρεος (Areos)</note> harms the Moon or Venus by rising after them, or by being in square or opposition, or when Venus or the Moon is alone, he does not necessarily take life away entirely, nor do the planets when declining; rather, they cause the mothers to be hampered only by **setbacks** or bodily weaknesses. However, if they are at the **centers** or at the **Ascending Node** <gloss>☊, also known as the Dragon's Head</gloss>, they make the mothers short-lived or subject to injuries.

### Signs of Mortality and the Mastery of Planets

...only a **short duration** <note>original: ὀλίγοχρονου (oligochronou)</note> specifically for those in simple motion, bringing about a fall or a downward course. One must contribute the assessment of the powers toward its own growth from those stars that follow, especially if they are excluded or blocked. By the **fatal omens** <note>original: θανασίμοις τεκμηρίοις (thanasimois tekmēriois)</note> and those signs of **wasting** <note>original: φθινώδεσι (phthinōdesi) — referring to consumption or chronic decline</note>, the text makes the examination concerning the **vision** <note>original: ὄψεις (opseis)</note>. For they are **repulsive** <note>original: ἀποκρουστικὰς (apokroustikas)</note> to those who are wounded or to those with **impairments** <note>original: ἀποκεκωσμένοις (apokekwōmenois) — a term often used for being deafened, dulled in the senses, or physically blunted</note> or similar conditions. 

The analysis also examines **incisions** <note>original: τομὰς (tomas) — surgical cuts</note> and **cauterizations** of the parts or even those occurring through the **veins** <note>original: φλέβας (phlebas)</note>. In fatal cases, this configuration produces **feverish conditions** <note>original: πυρετικοὺς (pyretikous)</note>. Everything that fails or expires happens as if by **sudden** and violent forces. One must take these factors into account beforehand. The **hearth** <note>original: ἑστία (hestia) — the focal point or symbolic center</note> of the matter is the death resulting from birth-circumstances or sufferings. Furthermore, one must observe the **days** especially, and the **Sun** and the **Moon**, such as:

Only the degree of the western horizon is destructive, because the **Lord of Life** is made to disappear there <note>referring to the Sun or the Releasor setting below the earth</note>.

As for the stars testifying <note>forming an aspect</note> from under the earth in this way: they only subtract <note>years from the life-span</note>, provided you observe them joining the paths of the **Releasor** until the **Releasor** sets. This does not prevent it, because the star does not bring itself to the **releasing** place, but rather brings the Releasor to its own places. 

And so that we may know: the **benefics** <term>agathopoioi</term> <note>Jupiter and Venus</note> subtract <note>In this context, they "subtract" from the destructive power, thereby adding years</note>, while the **malefics** <term>kakopoioi</term> <note>Saturn and Mars</note> [subtract from the life-span]. This also applies to **Mercury** <term>Hermes</term> <note>represented by the symbol ☿</note> in all cases, whichever of them he is configured with toward the preceding degree. 

The number for the addition or subtraction is determined through each degree: however many the **seasonal hours** of that specific degree happen to be. If it is day, one uses the hours of the day; if it is night, the hours of the night. This is based on the total sum of each of the complete hours. One must proceed according to the rising of those hours and subtract according to the proportion of the departure, until the division or dissolution reaches the 45th point toward the west. Regarding the sect of the following signs: both the places and the times of the **malefics** are **destructive**, whether they are the winding-intervals <note>original: "elissomatias" — likely referring to the paths of the planets</note> of the same or their rays.

# On the underlying circuit, containing [information] regarding risings and settings.

Since we are embarking on astrological matters, it is necessary to know more summarily the placement of every star in the zodiacal <insert>obliquely-</insert>moving circle <note>original: "zōdiakos kyklos" — the path the sun appears to follow, tilted relative to the equator</note>. This circle extends from the north and toward the south; there are 12 divisions, which are also called **zodiac signs** <note>original: "zōdia," literally "living beings" or "little animals"</note>. Their names are these: **Aries** (the Ram), **Taurus** (the Bull), **Gemini** (the Twins), **Cancer** (the Crab), **Leo** (the Lion), **Virgo** (the Virgin), **Libra** (the Scales), **Scorpio** (the Scorpion), **Sagittarius** (the Archer), **Capricorn** (the Goat-Horned), **Aquarius** (the Water-Bearer), **Pisces** (the Fish). And in each of these seven heavenly zones, the seven spheres are called the subordinate positions of the **wandering stars** <note>original: "planōmenōn asterōn" — from which we get the word "planet"</note>. In the first and highest is **Saturn** <note>original: "Kronos"</note>; in the second, **Jupiter** <note>original: "Zeus"</note>; in the third, **Mars** <note>original: "Arēs"</note>; in the fourth, the **Sun**; in the fifth, **Venus** <note>original: "Aphroditē"</note>; in the sixth, **Mercury** <note>original: "Hermēs"</note>; and in the seventh or lowest, the **Moon**. They are named **planets** either as if from their "descents" or as if from their "paths," or because they make their own movement through the 12 signs in opposition to the motion of the heavens <note>Ancient astronomers observed that while the whole sky rotates east-to-west daily, the planets slowly "wander" west-to-east through the zodiac</note>. The planets are 7. <gloss>Ch Ch</gloss> <note>Scribal marks, possibly shorthand for "checked" or a religious invocation</note> But the fixed stars are 48. Their names are: the **Great Bear** (Ursa Major), **Cepheus**, the **Little Bear** (Ursa Minor), the **Horse** (Pegasus), the **Serpent** (Draco), with which there are also seven [others]: the **Hare** (Lepus), **Perseus**, the **Sea-Monster** (Cetus), **Andromeda**, **Orion**, the **Charioteer** (Auriga), the **Centaurs**, the **Crow** (Corvus), the **Water-Jar** (Crater), the **She-Goat** (Capella), the **Kid**, the **Kneeler** (Hercules), the **Lyre**, the **Northern Crown**, **Argo** [the Ship], the **Southern Crown**, the **River Eridanus**, which is also <gloss>said to be</gloss> cloudy.

# The Solar Path and the Length of Days

The circle—the solar circle—touches all the **twelve signs of the zodiac** <term>original: "ιβ ζωδίοις" (12 zōdiois) — the "living figures" or constellations along the sun's path</term> around the pole. It creates the interval of the days. Because of this, it causes the day at the **summer solstice** <term>original: "therinē tropē" — literally the "summer turn," when the sun reaches its highest point</term> to be the longest.

In this [solstice], as the sun descends toward the southern parts, it provides the favorable regions with a smaller <unclear>portion</unclear> <note>original: "moir," likely an abbreviation for "moira," meaning degrees of a circle</note> of the day, so that the longest day exceeds the shortest day by six hours.

And the half-hour before is less than the second hour. These additions of hours occur during the summer month relative to the hour and a half. Thus, the **solar circle** <term>original: "hēliakos kyklos"</term> is understood as **eccentric** <term>original: "ekkentros" — an astronomical concept where the center of the sun's orbit is not the center of the Earth</term> if it is divided into twelve by the zodiac circle. 

These are unequal segments of the zodiac <unclear>remaining</unclear> where the smallest [parts] are among these. It is therefore said that when the sun is found in the segment of **Cancer** <term>original: "karkinos" — the crab</term>, it especially produces the longest day, consisting of 18 **equinoctial hours** <term>original: "isēmerinōn" — hours of equal length, as opposed to seasonal hours which changed with the time of year</term>. 

For there, the night [is short] because of the time and the light of the season of Cancer. Concerning the island called **Thule** <note>A legendary northern land, often identified by ancient geographers as the edge of the known world, possibly modern-day Iceland, Norway, or the Shetland Islands</note>, it is said that the day is [continuous]. Wherever the sun might be on this island—which is an **arctic** <term>original: "arktikē" — northern, or "belonging to the Bear"</term> island—it shines upon them from the east; for this reason, they are within the **arctic circle** <term>original: "arktikou kyklou"</term>.

Therefore, if someone should **take to their bed** <note>original: "kataklithē" — falling ill or being confined to bed</note> during the days having light <note>The "illuminated" days marked with a plus sign in the margin</note>, he will be saved, whether it happens quickly or slowly. One must know that some days of the **moon** are illuminated, while others are unilluminated. <meta>While the previous page focused on the "Sphere of Democritus" and medical prognosis based on the lunar cycle, this page shifts to a technical astronomical description of the sun’s movement through the zodiac. # Concerning the entrance and the cycle of the sun through the zodiac signs.

Since the 12 zodiac signs govern just like regions, the sun <note>original symbol: $\odot$</note> dwells within them as if in houses. The first sign is Aries <term>Aries ♈</term>, and the sun enters it on the 15th of the month of March, at the <unclear>1st</unclear> hour of the night. It remains in this sign for 30 days and 6 hours. <note>The addition of 6 hours to each 30-day stay accounts for the 365.24-day solar year, eventually requiring a leap year.</note> Departing from there, it enters Taurus <term>Taurus ♉</term> on the 19th of April, at the 11th hour of the night, and stays within it for 30 days and 6 hours. It departs and enters Gemini <term>Gemini ♊</term> on the 19th of May, at the 9th hour of the day. Having spent the same amount of time there, it departs and enters Cancer <term>Cancer ♋</term> on the 19th of the month of June, at the 7th hour of the night. From there it departs and enters Leo <term>Leo ♌</term> on the 19th of the month of July, at the 5th hour of the day. Departing from there, it enters Virgo <term>Virgo ♍</term> on the 19th of the month of August. Departing from there, it enters Libra <term>Libra ♎</term> on the 10th of the month of September, at the 1st hour of the day. Having gone out from there, it goes away into Scorpio <term>Scorpio ♏</term> on the 11th of the month of October, at the 7th hour. Having done the same, it enters Sagittarius <term>Sagittarius ♐</term> on the 11th of the month of November, at the 9th hour of the night. On the 11th it departs and enters Capricorn <term>Capricorn ♑</term> on the 11th of the month of December, at the 6th hour of the day. Again, it enters Aquarius <term>Aquarius ♒</term> on the 11th of the month of January, at the 5th hour of the day. And again, it enters Pisces <term>Pisces ♓</term> on the 11th of the month of February, at the 10th hour of the night. Having spent the appointed time in it—namely 30 days and 6 hours—it returns again from there to Aries <term>Aries ♈</term> on the 15th of March, at the hour of <unclear>dawn</unclear> <note>literally: "early morning of the night"</note>. And thus the sun travels in a cycle throughout the ages by the command of the Creator God, who created the—

->universe.<-

# + Land Measurement <note>original: Γεωδαισία (Geodaisia)</note> with the proofs in the name of Heron
# and brief and varied measurements

A point <term>Semeion; the most basic unit of geometry</term> is that which has no part. A line is a breadthless length. The extremities of a line are points. A straight line is a line which lies evenly with the points on itself. A surface <term>Epiphaneia; a 2D area</term> is that which has length and width only. The extremities of a surface are lines. A plane surface is a surface which lies evenly with the straight lines on itself. A plane angle is the inclination to one another of two lines in a plane which meet one another and do not lie in a straight line. And when the lines containing the angle are straight, the angle is called rectilinear. When a straight line standing on another straight line makes the adjacent angles equal to one another, each of the equal angles is a right angle, and the straight line standing on the other is called a perpendicular to that on which it stands. An obtuse angle is that which is greater than a right angle. An acute angle is that which is less than a right angle. A boundary is that which is an extremity of anything. A figure is that which is contained by any boundary or boundaries. A circle is a plane figure contained by one line, which is called the circumference <note>original: περιφέρεια (periphery)</note>, such that all straight lines falling upon it from one point among those lying within the figure [are equal to one another]... <note>The Greek text cuts off here mid-definition.</note>

A diameter of a circle is any straight line drawn through the center and terminated in both directions by the circumference of the circle; this line also bisects the circle. A semicircle is the shape contained by the diameter and the arc <note>original: περιφερείας (periphereias)</note> cut off by it. A segment of a circle is the shape contained by a straight line and a circular arc, whether that arc is larger or smaller than a semicircle. Rectilinear figures are those bounded by straight lines: three-sided figures are those bounded by three lines, four-sided by four, and many-sided <term>Polypleura; what we now call polygons</term> are those bounded by more than four lines. Among three-sided shapes, an equilateral triangle is one having three equal sides, an isosceles triangle has only two equal sides, and a scalene <term>Skalenon; literally "uneven" or "limping"</term> triangle has three unequal sides. Furthermore, among three-sided shapes, a right-angled triangle is one that has a right angle, an obtuse-angled triangle has one obtuse angle, and an acute-angled triangle has three acute angles. Among four-sided shapes, a square is that which is both equilateral and right-angled; an oblong <note>original: ἑτερόμηκες (heteromēkes), literally "other-length," referring to a rectangle</note> is right-angled but not equilateral; a rhombus is equilateral but not right-angled; and a rhomboid <note>original: ῥομβοειδές (rhomboeides)</note> is that which has its opposite sides and angles equal to one another, but is neither equilateral nor right-angled. **P**lane Geometry is composed of the point, the line,

From the final product, take the square root <note>original: "τετραγωνικὴν πλευρὰν" — literally the "square side," which is the historical term for a square root.</note>. This will be the area.

## How non-right-angled triangles may be transformed through right-angled ones and applied to them

<image-desc>Geometric diagram featuring a horizontal baseline with points labeled α (left), η (middle), and β (right). A vertical line segment extends upwards from point η to point γ. A second, diagonal line segment also originates from point η and extends upwards towards the left. This visualizes the concept of a perpendicular (κάθετος) versus an oblique line on a base.</image-desc>

In the study of geometric parts and in the diagrams themselves, much consideration is required, not only concerning the quantities of the side measurements but also the differences between the angles. For right angles do not differ from non-right angles in a simple way; rather, non-right angles fall far from the truth if one were to treat them as if they were right angles. An angle is <term>called</term> <note>original: "λ[έγεται]" (legetai)</note> **right** when a <term>perpendicular</term> <note>original: "κάθετος" (kathetos) — a line falling at a 90-degree angle.</note> dropped toward the **base** <note>original: "βάσις" (basis)</note> creates right angles with that base. For example, let the **base** be *α β*, and the perpendicular dropped from a point above be *η γ*. In this case, the angles *γ η α* and *γ η β* are right angles.

## On the Circles of the Heaven

There are certain circles conceived in the heaven which also possess
a nomenclature; [they are perceived] only by sensible forms. These either
all take a single [position]. They are these: the ho-
rizon, the meridian, and the Equator <note>original: Ισημερινός (Isemerinos) — "equal day," the circle where day and night are equal.</note>, and in addition to these
the Milky Way <note>original: Γαλαξίας (Galaxias).</note>. Some are rather [calculated] into numbers from the
northern circles, and [pass] through us rather than through the whole sphere;
they refer to the zones that have been straightened
appearing to us as phenomena. But that mist <note>likely referring to the appearance of the Milky Way or atmospheric refraction</note>
of the sight is truncated <note>original: κολοβός (kolobos) — in Greek astronomy, this describes circles that are cut off by the horizon and are not visible in their entirety.</note>; just as toward the south pole
the form does not incline to a shadow. And the [circle] from the beginning
from the south and through us as toward the north pole
is not entirely truncated; it was thus conceived [as] 2.
For those dwelling [in the north], these things pertain. But the south [is] for those dwelling
opposite <note>referring to the inhabitants of the southern hemisphere or antipodes.</note>.
